title: Best Laptop Deals (Black Friday 2026)
summary: 5 laptops worth buying this Black Friday, why each one is worth it, and the October 2026 prices to beat.
intro: {deal_hook} on top laptops. Check each offer before you buy.
We picked 5 laptops for different budgets. Prices can change or sell out at any time, so check the current price and the exact configuration before you buy.
method: Picks come from 2026 hands-on reviews (Tom's Hardware, PCWorld, Tom's Guide, Digital Trends, Notebookcheck, MobileSyrup) and October 2026 deal roundups (TechRadar, GamesRadar, Memeburn). Prices shown are the deal prices those roundups reported on Oct 15, 2026, at the retailer named. They change often and the retailer may not be Amazon, so treat each as a price to beat, not a promise. The Amazon buttons search for the model, so compare the exact configuration before you buy.
assumptions: no price is guaranteed on Black Friday itself. We will update this guide when real Black Friday deals go live.

products.name: Apple MacBook Air 13-inch (M5)
why: The MacBook Air keeps the formula reviewers have recommended for years and makes it faster. It is fanless, so it stays silent, and it weighs about 2.7 pounds, which is easy to carry all day. The base model now starts with 16GB of memory and 512GB of storage, so you do not need to pay extra for a usable setup.

Tom's Hardware calls it still the best Mac laptop for most people. Digital Trends says you can stop worrying about performance and calls it one of the easiest laptop recommendations in years, especially if you are coming from an old Windows laptop or an Intel Mac.
specs: Apple M5 chip, fanless design
13.6-inch Liquid Retina display, 2560 x 1664
16GB memory and 512GB storage in the base model
2 Thunderbolt 4 ports, MagSafe charging, headphone jack, Wi-Fi 7
Apple claims up to 18 hours of battery; Pickr saw 6 to 10 hours in daily use
pros: Fast enough that most people will not outgrow it
Keyboard and trackpad rated among the best
cons: The MacBook Neo costs almost half as much
Apple's 18-hour battery figure is a best case
Tom's Hardware notes the new base specs make it slightly pricier
products.best_for: Students, office workers, programmers and anyone who wants one laptop for years.
products.skip_if: you need Windows-only software, or you just want the lowest price.
products.deal_note: Memeburn names it the best MacBook to watch this Black Friday. Last holiday season the older M4 Air fell to $750 at Amazon (CNN Underscored), so an M5 deal is the one to wait for.
products.amazon_listing: Apple 2026 MacBook Air 13-inch Laptop with M5 chip: Built for AI, 13.6-inch Liquid Retina
products.desc: A fanless 13.6-inch MacBook Air with the Apple M5 chip, 16GB of memory and 512GB of storage in the base model. It does not run Windows-only software.
products.benefit: Picture a student or office worker carrying a 2.7-pound laptop all day that stays silent in a quiet library. Digital Trends calls it one of the easiest laptop recommendations in years, and the base model now starts with 16GB of memory. It has twice the base memory of the MacBook Neo in this guide. The catch: the MacBook Neo costs almost half as much, and Apple's 18-hour battery claim is a best case, since Pickr saw 6 to 10 hours in daily use.

products.name: Apple MacBook Neo
why: The MacBook Neo is Apple's cheapest Mac. It uses a phone chip (the A18 Pro) to hit the price, but it still feels like a real MacBook, with an aluminum body, a bright 13-inch screen and a good keyboard and trackpad.

In Tom's Guide's web-surfing test it lasted 13 hours and 28 minutes, and the screen measured 452 nits. For browsing, streaming, writing and schoolwork, that is plenty. The catch is the 8GB of memory, which is the only option.
specs: Apple A18 Pro chip, 8GB memory (only option)
256GB storage in the base model
13-inch Liquid Retina display, 2408 x 1506, up to 500 nits
36.5Wh battery, 20W charging
1080p camera, aluminum body
pros: Long battery life for the price
cons: No True Tone and no wide color (P3) display
Only one USB-C port supports an external display
The 256GB model has no Touch ID, per MobileSyrup
products.best_for: Students and first-time Mac buyers who mostly browse, stream and write.
products.skip_if: you keep dozens of tabs open, edit video, or run heavy apps.
products.deal_note: It is already $100 below its $699 list price at Apple. It is the same laptop at every store, so compare Apple, Amazon and Best Buy before buying.
products.amazon_listing: Apple 2026 MacBook Neo 13-inch Laptop with A18 Pro chip: Built for AI and Apple Intelligen
products.desc: Apple's cheapest Mac, with an A18 Pro chip and 8GB of memory as the only option. It has no Touch ID on the 256GB model, per MobileSyrup.
products.benefit: Picture a student writing essays, browsing and streaming between classes on a real MacBook. It lasted 13 hours 28 minutes in Tom's Guide's web-surfing test, and the screen measured 452 nits. It is the cheapest way to get macOS in this guide. The catch: 8GB of memory is the only option, which limits heavy multitasking.

products.name: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x
why: The IdeaPad Slim 3x runs on a Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip, which is why it can last all day on a charge at such a low price. It is one of the cheapest Copilot+ PCs you can buy, and reviewers describe it as a simple everyday laptop for browsing, streaming and notes.

PCWorld praises its battery life and day-to-day speed but warns that the hardware makes a lot of compromises. The 15-inch screen is the weakest part, and the body is aluminum on top with plastic underneath. At this price, those trade-offs are easier to accept.
specs: Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip with 45 TOPS NPU (Copilot+ PC)
15.3-inch 1920 x 1200 IPS display
Up to 14 hours of battery, Rapid Charge gives about 2 hours from a 15-minute charge, per Lenovo
Configurations vary, so check RAM and storage on the exact listing
pros: Very long battery life for the price
Big 15-inch screen with a number pad
cons: The screen is the weakest part
ARM chip, so check that your apps support Windows on ARM
Below the IdeaPad Slim 5x, which one reviewer calls the best Windows laptop under $1,000
products.best_for: Everyday browsing, schoolwork and office tasks on a tight budget.
products.skip_if: you need gaming, color-accurate photo work, or specialized Windows software.
products.deal_note: Match the configuration, not just the model name. A cheaper listing with less RAM or storage is not the same deal.
products.amazon_listing: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3X - 2025 - Everyday AI Laptop - Copilot+ PC - 15.3" WUXGA Display - 1
products.desc: A 15.3-inch Windows laptop with a Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip and a 45 TOPS NPU, sold as a Copilot+ PC. It is not for gaming or color-accurate photo work.
products.benefit: Picture a laptop for notes and browsing that lasts all day without a charger. Lenovo claims up to 14 hours, and Rapid Charge gives about 2 hours from a 15-minute charge, per Lenovo. It is the budget Windows pick in this guide. The catch: PCWorld says the 15-inch screen is the weakest part, and the ARM chip may not run every app.

products.name: HP OmniBook X Flip 14
why: The OmniBook X Flip folds back 360 degrees, so it works as a laptop, a tablet or a stand for video. Magnets hold the screen steady in tablet mode, it supports a stylus, and the webcam has a privacy shutter. Reviewers praise the design and the comfortable keyboard.

The display is where you must be careful. HP sells three screens: 1920 x 1200 IPS, 1920 x 1200 60Hz OLED and a sharper 2880 x 1800 120Hz OLED. PCWorld and Tom's Hardware found the middle OLED dim and reflective, while the 2880 x 1800 panel looks excellent.
specs: 14-inch touchscreen, 360-degree hinge
Three display options (IPS, 60Hz OLED, 120Hz OLED)
59Wh battery; Tom's Guide measured about 8.5 hours in one configuration
Upgradeable SSD, Wi-Fi card and battery, per Tom's Hardware
Optional stylus, privacy-shutter webcam
pros: Flexible design for notes, sketching and travel
The best display option is excellent
cons: The 60Hz OLED option is dim and glare-prone
products.best_for: Note-takers, students and travelers who want a laptop and tablet in one.
products.skip_if: you need a bright screen outdoors, or you plan to game or edit video.
products.deal_note: Memeburn says an earlier $699 offer is the better price to beat, because the advertised discount overstates the real saving. Check which display your deal includes.
products.amazon_listing: HP OmniBook X Flip 14 2-in-1 Touchscreen Laptop, Ultra 5 226V, 32GB RAM | 14" WUXGA, Intel
products.desc: A 14-inch touchscreen laptop with a 360-degree hinge and three display options. The stylus is optional.
products.benefit: Picture a note-taker sketching a diagram in tablet mode at a lecture, then folding the screen back to type. Magnets hold the screen steady in tablet mode, the webcam has a privacy shutter, and Tom's Hardware says the SSD, Wi-Fi card and battery can be upgraded. It is the only 2-in-1 in this guide. The catch: PCWorld and Tom's Hardware found the middle OLED option dim and reflective, so choose the display carefully.

products.name: Lenovo LOQ 15 (RTX 5060)
why: The LOQ is Lenovo's budget gaming line, and the RTX 5060 model is built around its graphics card. PCWorld describes the LOQ 15 as effectively a portable RTX 5060, paired with a Ryzen 7 250, a 15.6-inch 1080p 144Hz screen and a 60Wh battery. Notebookcheck rates its 1080p gaming performance as very strong.

Be careful with the price. Notebookcheck says RTX 5060 laptops usually cost around $1,200, so the $650 off is measured against an inflated list price. GamesRadar's roundup also listed gaming laptops starting around $899 to $939 at Walmart, Best Buy and Amazon, so compare before paying.

AMD Ryzen 7 250 processor
15.6-inch 1080p IPS display, 144Hz
60Wh battery

cons: Battery life is short, per PCWorld

products.best_for: Gamers who want a current graphics card for 1080p gaming without flagship prices.
products.skip_if: you want long battery life away from a charger, or 1440p gaming.
products.deal_note: The $1,199.99 price is close to the usual RTX 5060 price, not a standout discount. Wait for a lower price, or compare against other RTX 5060 laptops.

products.benefit: Picture a gamer playing at 1080p at a desk near an outlet. Notebookcheck rates its 1080p gaming performance as very strong, and PCWorld describes it as effectively a portable RTX 5060. It is the only gaming laptop in this guide. The catch: PCWorld says battery life is short, and Notebookcheck says the list price it is compared with looks inflated for RTX 5060 laptops.

tips.title: How to spot a real laptop deal
items: Compare with the lowest recent price,
not the crossed-out list price. Memeburn warns that Black Friday discounts often look bigger than they are.
RAM, storage, screen type and graphics power can differ between two listings with the same name, as the LOQ and OmniBook above show.
Aim for 16GB of memory on Windows laptops.
8GB is workable on a MacBook Neo for light use, but reviewers call it a real limit on Windows.
GamesRadar warned that some early gaming deals could sell out quickly.
before you buy, especially for a laptop you cannot test in a store.

faq: Black Friday is Friday, November 27, 2026, and Cyber Monday is Monday, November 30.
Should I buy now or wait for Black Friday?

TechRadar notes retailers may be holding back some of their best laptop deals until Black Friday. GamesRadar found some early deals already near typical Black Friday prices. If a laptop you want is already at a price you are happy with, buying now is reasonable.
Is the Amazon price the same as Best Buy?
Not always. Several deals above were reported at Best Buy or Apple. Use the Amazon button to compare the current price and the exact configuration.
For light browsing and schoolwork on the MacBook Neo, reviewers say yes. For heavy multitasking or Windows laptops, 16GB is the safer choice.

verdict.line: If you want one laptop deal that suits most people, get this one: Tom's Hardware still calls it the best Mac laptop for most people, and it now starts with 16GB of memory. The MacBook Neo costs almost half as much, and Apple's 18-hour battery claim is a best case.
